# Survey design, weights and standard errors {#c05-survey-design}

MICS is a **complex sample survey**. To produce correct population estimates and standard errors, an analysis needs to account for the survey design.

For the MICS6 selected-child (`fs`) data, three pieces of information are central:

```text
fsweight   sampling weight for the selected child
PSU        primary sampling unit
stratum    sampling stratum
```

The standard MICS6 files include these variables in the `fs` dataset. IPUMS also harmonises the corresponding survey-design variables. See the [IPUMS MICS variable-name crosswalk](https://mics.ipums.org/mics/resources/training_exercises/2024_12_var_names_ipums_unicef.pdf).

::: {.alternativebox-header}
**The basic rule**
:::

::: {.alternativebox}
For analysis of children in the `fs` file, do not calculate a weighted mean and then use an ordinary standard error. Tell the software about the **weight, clustering and stratification together**.
:::

This section explains:

- what the selected-child weight represents;
- why clustering and stratification matter;
- how to set up a MICS6 survey design in R and Stata;
- how to estimate subpopulations correctly; and
- what changes when several countries/surveys are combined.

## Why ordinary standard errors are wrong

MICS does not draw children independently from a simple random sample.

Households are selected through a stratified, clustered sample design. Children living in the same sampled cluster can be more similar to one another than children selected independently from across the country.

If the analysis ignores that structure, the estimated **standard errors, confidence intervals and p-values can be wrong**.

Weights solve a different problem. They account for unequal selection probabilities and survey adjustments. They do not, by themselves, tell the software how observations are clustered or stratified.

A correct design-based analysis therefore needs:

```text
WEIGHT
  +
PSU / CLUSTER
  +
STRATUM
```

## The three design variables

### `fsweight`

`fsweight` is the sample weight for the randomly selected child aged 5–17.

Use it when the unit of analysis is the selected child — including analyses of foundational reading and numeracy among children aged 7–14.

### `PSU`

`PSU` identifies the **primary sampling unit** used for sampling-error estimation.

In most MICS applications this corresponds to the sampled cluster/enumeration area.

Do not assume that the household identifier is the PSU.

### `stratum`

`stratum` identifies the sampling stratum used for variance estimation.

Stratification is part of the sample design and should be incorporated when estimating standard errors.

The exact design variables should always be checked in the country dataset and survey documentation. Some surveys contain additional working design variables, but standard MICS6 releases generally provide `PSU` and `stratum`.
